Subject: ACME - Order Form SLA redlines (maintenance & P1 response)

Hi Kimberly,

Attached are our proposed redlines to the Order Form and SLA. Two points we want to call out up front:
- P1 response time: we need a guaranteed initial response within 30 minutes and an engineer-assigned update within 2 hours for Severity 1 incidents.
- Maintenance windows: we are asking to limit rolling maintenance to a single 4-hour weekly window with a 72-hour advance notice; we cannot accept overnight rolling maintenance.

On credits: we proposed a 5% monthly service credit for availability falling below 99.5%, increasing to 15% if below 98%. We want the credit to be applied pro rata and capped at one full monthly invoice.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the P1 timelines as written or propose an alternative allocation (e.g., initial 30 min response + triage/update within 4 hours), and whether you have flexibility on the maintenance window language.

Kim / Samantha —

Draft language below for the Order Form and MSA. I attached a doc with tracked changes (redline_suggestion.docx). Key legal positions:

- P1 Response: Replace your proposed "engineer-assigned update within 2 hours" with "initial acknowledgment within 30 minutes and substantive update within 4 hours; Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to assign an engineer within 2 hours."

- Availability Credit: Amend to a sliding credit table tied to monthly uptime (UTC):
  * 99.9% - 100%: 0% credit
  * 99.5% - 99.899%: 5% credit
  * 98.0% - 99.499%: 10% credit
  * <98.0%: 20% credit (capped at one monthly invoice)
  Credits apply only to fees for the affected service and require a claim within 30 days.

- Maintenance windows: Define a single weekly 4-hour maintenance window by region. Rolling maintenance permitted only for critical security fixes with 72-hour notice and customer opt-out for scheduled major upgrades. We will exclude agreed blackout dates submitted 30 days in advance.

Please confirm if ACME can accept the claim window and the credit caps; if they prefer a flat percentage instead of a sliding table, flag which thresholds they'd like.

Lauren Bishop
